column1: # Deliberate differences between sources/yomitan.json and Yomitan's Spanish rules at d3c54c1 (docs/languages.md 8.2), checked by tools/check-yomitan.mjs.

column7: Yomitan's stem-change rules test X([a-z]*)ending$ but replace the first X of the text (term.replace(/i/, 'e')), even one that a letter outside [a-z] follows; the pack's stemChange changes the first X that the rule's [a-z]* reaches. Neither output is a word (británico -> bretánicir in Yomitan, británecir in the pack).

For a text that starts with jue, the -ar rules of Yomitan's imperative and present subjunctive change ue to u and then replace (a|ue|uen)$ or (ue|ues|ue|uen)$, endings they do not test, so juegen gives jugen, which a regular rule then reads as jugar. The pack has the branch only for the endings that give an infinitive.

Yomitan's reflexive rule matches the pronoun anywhere in the text and replaces every match (ya me levantar -> ya levantarse), with any white space after it; the pack's pattern rules are anchored on the pronoun and a space at the start of the text, where a lookup that starts at the pronoun puts it (the pack's NFKC processor turns a no-break space into a space first).
